payload.goal: Stop sofar disowning its own statusline: refreshInterval is the documented fix for a frozen idle line (Claude Code re-runs the command only on session start / new message / compact / mode toggle), but adding it makes isSofarStatusline's exact-2-key test fail, so install reports 'kept' and uninstall reports 'foreign' on sofar's own entry. Ship refreshInterval in the installed entry and widen the identity test to tolerate that one tunable key, keeping the theirs-wins law for genuinely foreign lines and keeping legacy 2-key installs removable.

payload.because: The two halves were in direct contradiction. refreshInterval is Claude Code's own documented cure for a frozen idle line — the host re-runs a statusLine command only on session start, new assistant message, compact and mode toggles — but under exact-key-count identity, setting it turned sofar's own entry foreign: --uninstall refused to remove it and --install refused to touch it, both telling the user to hand-edit. So the prescribed fix silently broke the uninstall path, reproduced live against 0.23.0. Shipping the key by default removes the discovery burden entirely; widening identity keeps the theirs-wins law intact where it matters (a different command is still someone else's) while an allowlist rather than a blanket accept means an unfamiliar key still counts as customization we must not delete.
payload.chose: D1: statusline identity is type + command, tolerating exactly one tunable key (refreshInterval), and the installed entry ships refreshInterval: 10. isSofarStatusline matches on type + command and requires every remaining key to be in an owned set {type, command, refreshInterval}; any other extra key (e.g. padding) is still foreign. This recognizes both the legacy two-key entry installed before the key shipped and a user-retuned interval.
payload.over: Keeping byte-for-byte identity (Object.keys(v).length === 2) and documenting refreshInterval as a manual edit users make at their own risk; or accepting any object whose command is ours regardless of extra keys.
payload.rule: statusLine identity is type + command plus the owned-key allowlist — never reintroduce an exact key-count test, and add a key to STATUSLINE_OWN_KEYS only when sofar itself writes it.

tasks.title: isSofarStatusline: match on type + command against an owned-key allowlist; STATUSLINE_SETTINGS_ENTRY ships refreshInterval: 10
Tests: retuned interval removable, legacy 2-key removable, foreign command still refused, our command + unowned key still refused
SPEC §CLI init --statusline entry bytes + uninit matching clause; uninit.ts comments; README refreshInterval note
Release: bump sofar.sh to 0.24.0 and publish (user runs npm publish)

payload.note: 0.24.0 published to npm and installed globally (sofar --version = 0.24.0). Verified live against the installed engine using a copy of the real ~/.claude/settings.json: the 3-key entry with refreshInterval: 10 is recognized as ours and removed, other top-level keys preserved.

payload.text:
FINDING 2026-08-08: the statusline already HOLDS the silent-misroute signal and does not call it out.

Observed live: the line read `sofar · record-index · ● peer-messaging 5/5` — branch segment and initiative segment naming different things, while the session had been working record-index for hours. Not a bug. statusline.ts resolves session-first by design ("the session's registered home wins over the branch, so closing an initiative — which unbinds every branch pointing at it — leaves THIS session's line intact until it ends"), which is right for the close case it was built for.

Why it went stale: one long Claude Code session (9e94756b) started on drift-certification, re-registered on peer-messaging, then did all later work under FRESHLY MINTED sofar session ids rather than re-adopting its own. The statusline is keyed on the CLAUDE CODE session id — the only id the host hands it — so it can only report the home of the registration sharing that id, which froze while the work moved on. doctor independently flags the same session: "spans 3 initiatives (torn, history): drift-certification, peer-messaging, writeback-collisions".

The opportunity: when the session's registered home DISAGREES with the branch binding, that is exactly the condition repo-memory M3 says doctor cannot detect — "events landing uniformly in one WRONG initiative are byte-identical to correct work". doctor cannot see it because both records look correct. The statusline CAN, for free, because it already computes both values and prints them side by side. Today it renders the disagreement and leaves the reader to notice; a reader who assumes the two segments agree reads right past it.

Proposal (unbuilt, needs a decision): mark the disagreement rather than merely displaying it — a distinct glyph or tone on the initiative segment when home != branch binding, meaning "your writes are pinned somewhere other than where your branch points". Cheap: both values are already in hand, no extra fold, no extra I/O, so speed T2 is untouched. Must stay a MARK and not a warning — a long session that deliberately keeps its home while checking out branches is legitimate, and the CLI output law keeps semantic tone reserved.

Writing to another initiative with an explicit `initiative` argument TEARS the calling session. sofar_add_note/log_decision/update_task all accept `initiative`, and using one from a session pinned elsewhere lands events where that session is not registered — doctor reports it as "spans N initiatives (torn/leaked)". Observed 2026-08-08: session 9e94756b was registered in drift-certification and peer-messaging, and its notes written with initiative:"writeback-collisions" made it span 3. The explicit argument is for READING another record or for a one-off write you accept the tear for; the clean pattern for real work in a second initiative is a SEPARATE pinned session — sofar_start_session({initiative}) → write → sofar_end_session — which is also what repo-memory M3 already requires for a session working a different initiative than its branch. Corollary for long sessions: re-adopting your own Claude Code session id on each start_session keeps `sofar statusline` accurate, because that line is keyed on the HOST's session id and can only report the home of the registration sharing it; minting fresh ids per work batch freezes the statusline at the first home while the work moves on.

payload.next_action: Decide whether to mark home != branch-binding disagreement on the statusline initiative segment (a mark, never a warning — both values are already in hand, so no fold or I/O cost).
payload.summary: Diagnosed a statusline reading `record-index` as branch but `peer-messaging` as initiative. Not a bug — session-first resolution working as designed; the session's home froze because a long Claude Code session minted fresh sofar ids per work batch instead of re-adopting its own. Recorded the finding that the statusline already holds the silent-misroute signal (home != branch binding) that doctor structurally cannot detect, plus repo memory on the cross-initiative write pattern that tears sessions.
